rules.knownGap: These patterns are English-only and DO NOT cover the other 15 locales. The same claim is live in Spanish as "solo puedes ver y editar la tuya" and in Japanese as "表示や編集ができるのは、あなた自身の金庫だけです", and no English regex reaches either. A keyword grep is worse than useless here — es (aislada), ja (分離), nl (geïsoleerd), pl (odizolowany) and tr (yalıtılmıştır) share no root with `isolat`, so a grep reports 15 false gaps or 15 false passes depending on which way you point it. Localised copy is verified today by parsing the field per locale by hand. The durable fix is a field-level check (protections[-1], trustBand.proof[3] and friends each have one approved value per locale) rather than more regexes; tracked on ARY-1377.

rules.label: Paid-report sections presented as free-tier output
rules.guidance: These are fields of the PAID AdvisoryReport (advisoryPipeline.ts:133-145). The free AdvisoryEstimate carries only ranges, lineItems, costOfInaction and gapsInProtection — it has no riskAreas and no recommendedActions. This is a tier boundary, not a capability denial: the feature exists, it just is not free. Bare "considerations" and "next steps" are ordinary English and are only matched next to free-tier wording; the rest are literal field names and are matched anywhere. ARY-1369: sweep the phrase FAMILY over the CORPUS — a one-term grep closed ARY-1364 green while "recommended actions to take" was still live. ARY-1533 RULING (2026-07-29, Vault CMO): a forward-looking phrase used as a TOPIC the family reflects on is OUT of scope — e.g. "what happens next" coordinated with life-event nouns (inheritance, wills) and governed by a cognition verb (think about / plan ahead / get oriented around), paired with a free-tier marker. It names a subject the user thinks about, not a promise that the product will hand back the paid recommendedActions list, so it is allowed by design (live on home, features and the digital-estate-planning-checklist blog, en + 15 locales). What stays IN scope is a promise the product DELIVERS prescriptive, prioritized directives to the user: "your next steps", "what to do next", "recommended actions", "your action plan". Do NOT add "what happens next" to the patterns — it would false-positive on that live copy; "next steps" is already caught because it reads as the deliverable. Non-violation cleared thrice: ARY-1364 / -1369 / -1518.

rules.label: Encryption claimed over the record as a whole ("everything is encrypted")
rules.guidance: The app-layer seal is column-scoped (ARY-1322): value_band, institution, serialNumber, purchasePrice, tags and belongsTo are stored in plaintext. Transport (TLS) and the provider's at-rest disk encryption do cover everything, but a sentence that applies encryption to the record as a whole reads as an app-layer exhaustiveness claim, which is false. Name what is sealed.

rules.label: Support-access claim overstated as "no admin/support surface or internal tooling exists"
rules.guidance: C-025's claim survives; its first basis sentence does not. Three staff-authenticated read surfaces are LIVE in production — GET /api/analytics/{funnel,dashboard}, GET /api/feedback/{metrics,dashboard}, GET /api/client-errors/recent — gated by a shared bearer/Basic token (ANALYTICS_DASHBOARD_TOKEN, FEEDBACK_DASHBOARD_TOKEN, CLIENT_ERROR_READ_TOKEN), all three keys provisioned on the live prod API. So "no admin or support view exists" is false, and falsifiable in about two minutes by the exact sceptical reader /security is written for. The CTO countersign (ARY-1444) declines that sentence in EVERY locale. What is true is narrower and is what the row licenses: support cannot browse your vault, and no staff account type exists that could be given access — mobile_users has no role column, and none of the three dashboards queries the asset, document, evidence, valuation, draft or vault tables. NOTE the patterns deliberately exclude "account type" and bare "staff": "no staff account type exists" is the APPROVED half and must stay green. This rule is the copy-side twin of ARY-1473, which gates the code side (a future staff dashboard joining vault tables).

rules.label: A price or currency on the detailed advisory report
rules.guidance: ADDED 2026-10-06 (ARY-4291) off ARY-4252 §5, which found the price ban had NO machine-readable entry at all — thirteen rules ids and not one covering a price literal. 'Never a price' survived only as prose inside free-tier-paid-fields' `instead` guidance, which the build does not enforce, so the C-014 price ban was kept by human sweep alone. claims:sync could not catch the gap: its coverage check fires on RETIRED rows and C-014 is ✅. BOTH currencies are patterned deliberately. The live asset-vault-api-prod service is configured at REPORT_PRICE_MINOR=3999 / REPORT_PRICE_CURRENCY=USD — the price is $39.99, NOT £49 — so a £49-only pattern is UNDER-INCLUSIVE and would pass a page reading $39.99 (ARY-4252 §3.2). £49 is still patterned because it is the env default (env.ts:186,195) and the retired copy that shipped under it. Why a regex is safe here when C-018/C-020 needed notPatterned: there is no denial problem — we never argue against a price by quoting one, so the strings never appear in honest copy. The numeric patterns carry deliberate negative lookaheads so ordinary estate-planning figures stay green: £49 does not match inside £49,000 or £490, and nothing matches the £325,000 nil-rate band, £300 probate fees, a £490,000 home, or the app-level JSON-LD Offer price:'0' in src/config/structured-data.ts. The word 'premium' is deliberately NOT patterned — an insurance premium next to a currency is legitimate copy. PRODUCT-SIDE TWINS, not substitutes: asset-vault/src/lib/no-payment-surface.test.ts (web) and NoPaymentSurfaceTest (Android, ARY-1080) keep the price out of the product; this rule keeps it out of marketing. claims:check SCAN_ROOTS cannot see the product repo and those tests cannot see this one.

"zero-knowledge" and "end-to-end encrypted" appear legitimately and frequently as DENIALS in our honesty copy — /security says we deliberately do not claim them, in all 16 locales, and 15 blog posts repeat the disclaimer. A phrase-level regex would fire on the honest disclaimer far more often than on a real over-claim, which is the 'worse than nothing' failure mode this guard was built to avoid. Enforced by Brand & Trust review.

ADDED 2026-10-06 (ARY-4291) off ARY-4252 §5 — §0.1's standing rule is absolute (every prohibition is either a rules regex or a notPatterned entry, no third option and no silent omission) and this prohibition had neither; the reasoning below lived only as C-027 row prose, which the guard does not inherit. C-027 bans DENYING that Vaulto AI-estimates property and tangible value ("nothing auto-values your property", "user-maintained only", "no automated pricing", "it doesn't value anything for you"). A regex cannot express it because the banned framings are context-dependent: the identical words are TRUE and approved outside the revaluable set — "you record the mortgage yourself" (a liability, not revaluable), "Vaulto doesn't value pensions / investments / cash accounts", and the standing safe denials (no bank or lender link, no Land Registry link, no market feed, no automatic mortgage-balance pull). A phrase-level pattern would fire on those honest denials far more often than on a real over-claim — the same 'worse than nothing' failure mode that put C-018 and C-020 in this list. Enforced by the CMO claim gate plus the C-027 row itself, English-manual, like C-023. Precedent for how it fails in practice: the three real instances fixed on ARY-4261 (02af77b) were each a GLOBAL denial that happened to sweep property in alongside genuinely unvalued categories, which is a semantic scope error no regex detects.

ADDED 2026-10-06 (ARY-4316). The risk here is the INVERSE of a price leak, and it is context-dependent in exactly the way a regex cannot express. The banned shapes are (a) hardening the one-off into a permanence promise we do not honour -- 'pay once, free updates forever', 'never pay again', 'guaranteed for life' -- which would sweep in future SKUs and ignore revoke-on-refund, and (b) implying the report is purchasable today, or purchasable on the web at all (web has no card rail, ARY-830). Both are judgements about context and scope, not about a phrase. A regex on 'subscription' / 'one-time' / 'forever' would false-fire on precisely the sentences this row LICENSES -- 'not a subscription', 'you won't be charged again' are the product's own paywall compliance copy, shipped in 16 locales -- which is the same denial problem that made C-020, C-018/C-022 and C-027 notPatterned. The price leg needs no new regex: it is already enforced by the report-price rule under C-014. Enforced by the CMO gate plus this row (English-manual).
